subject: Final decision criteria & timing for hosting path selection - Medsprint MAP
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Tim O'Neil <tim.oneil@medsprint.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-20T09:18:00Z
Subject: Draft MAP & gating criteria for deployment mode + region

Hi Tim —

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Per our agreement I attached an updated Mutual Action Plan (Medsprint_MAP_v3.xlsx) that narrows the decision checkpoints we discussed into three concrete gates:

1) Evaluation & perf acceptance (SLOs for 95th pct tail latency and accuracy on the clinical prompts set)
2) Security & compliance gating (SOC2 items + data residency)
3) Procurement & cutover timeline (PO, network peering window, go/no-go)

Key tradeoffs to confirm by 9/10: Hosted (fastest start, lower ops burden) vs Dedicated (predictable throughput for our peak inference windows) vs Private (on-prem/VPC for PHI). We called out recommended region bindings based on traffic and latency: US-East for primary, US-West for DR.

Ask: Can you confirm whether PHI will be in-scope for the initial rollout? That drives whether Private becomes mandatory. If not PHI, we propose a staged path: Hosted for POC -> Dedicated reserved once traffic > X qps.

I also flagged a short technical checklist for your infra team; Karthik included comments inline. Proposed next steps in the MAP:
- Confirm scope (PHI Y/N) by 2027-08-27
- Schedule technical deep-dive (Karthik) week of 8/30
- Procurement target: PO by 9/23
- Pilot go-live window: 10/11–10/18

If that looks right I’ll push the MAP into the shared Drive and we can start the approvals track.

Best,
Alex

--
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

Subject: Re: Draft MAP & gating criteria for deployment mode + region

Alex —

Thanks for the clear next steps and the MAP. Quick answers from our side:
- PHI: yes, the initial rollout will include patient identifiers (lab results linked to patients) so PHI is in-scope.
- Compliance: our security team will need the SOC2 evidence; attaching their request separately.

Questions:
1) If PHI is in-scope, does Redwood require Private (VPC/on-prem) or can Dedicated (customer-dedicated GPUs with VPC peering) suffice?
2) Can you confirm the guaranteed retention of audit logs and whether those can be forwarded into our SIEM?

We can confirm scope formally by 8/27 but wanted to flag procurement timelines — finance tends to need 3 weeks post-final SOW. 9/23 PO target is tight but possible.

—Tim

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim O'Neil <tim.oneil@medsprint.com>, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-25T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & gating criteria for deployment mode + region

Team —

Technical notes for Medsprint (short):
- PHI in-scope: Private deployment is the only path that keeps all inference and keying inside customer-managed network if they require full airgap/HSM-backed KMS.
- Dedicated with VPC peering: acceptable for many PHI workloads if the customer controls egress rules and we sign a BAA + use customer-managed KMS. There are caveats: live KV-cache persistence and backup policies need explicit alignment.
- Hosted: not recommended for PHI unless you accept a dedicated tenancy + contractual encryption guarantees; still higher legal friction.

Recommended technical gating items to insert into MAP:
- KMS model for keys (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed)
- Audit-log forwarding endpoint (SIEM) and retention SLA (we can support 365 days export)
- Region pinning: primary US-East, with optional DR US-West. Cross-region replication for KV caches must be disabled for PHI.

I'll take the deep-dive call the week of 8/30. If procurement needs an explicit spec to attach to the SOW, I'll draft a short technical appendix by 9/1.

-Karthik

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim O'Neil <tim.oneil@medsprint.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T11:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & gating criteria for deployment mode + region

All —

PRIORITY NOTE for commercial team: given Medsprint's stated procurement window, we should present a low-friction path that minimizes legal/ops overhead so they can hit PO target. Suggested two-track offer in the MAP:
- Option A (fast): Hosted with customer-managed KMS + BAA addendum. Works if legal accepts shared tenancy with contractual assurances.
- Option B (compliant): Dedicated with VPC peering + customer KMS. Higher cost but clears most security asks.

Include clear migration language so Medsprint doesn't feel locked: "Start Hosted -> roll to Dedicated" clause and an estimated migration cost/time. This often speeds signatures.

I'll prepare the commercial language and the migration estimate today and add to the MAP.

-Marissa

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Tim O'Neil <tim.oneil@medsprint.com>, Jessica Park <jessica.park@medsprint.com>

Date: 2027-09-14T16:05:00Z
Subject: Final MAP update and agreed timeline (Hosted -> Dedicated fall-back)

Tim / Jessica —

Thanks for the review and for confirming PHI is in-scope. Per internal alignment we have updated the MAP in Drive and attached the following:
- Commercial: two-track offer (Hosted with customer-managed KMS + BAA) and Dedicated with VPC peering pricing tiers
- Technical appendix: KMS spec, audit-log forwarding endpoints, region pinning instructions (US-East primary)
- SOC2 evidence checklist for your security team (SOC2-evidence-request.pdf)

Agreed conditional path:
- Target: start pilot on Hosted (customer-managed KMS) with the understanding that production must be Dedicated if legal requires keys under customer control after SOW.
- Confirmation windows: scope (PHI) confirmed 8/27 (received), technical deep-dive completed 9/2, commercial final SOW signed by 9/24, PO by 9/30, pilot target 10/12.

Next actions (we've added these to the MAP):
1) Tim to share final SOC2 checklist responses by 9/18
2) Procurement to review draft SOW (Marissa will send SOW v1 today)
3) Karthik to provide the short tech appendix for SOW attachment (due 9/17)

If any of those dates are unworkable, flag here and we’ll adjust the MAP draft. Once SOW is signed we’ll lock the region binding and the Dedicated capacity commit if needed.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Alex
